Use `peter()` with a prompt to run a language model agent and receive a session. The agent can
inspect objects already loaded in your R environment, compute on them, and reuse named results
on later turns. Choosing an API, CLI or Ollama model changes the model route; its gptr R tool
still works in the selected live workspace. The model receives bounded descriptions and tool
results, which may include data values or plots, rather than an automatic serialization of
the full dataset. [Execution model](execution-model.html) explains copies, separate
workers and file-backed objects.

The same call works in a function, a loop or a script. This guide executes only scripted fake
providers; examples that connect to real services are shown without running them.

## Choose and connect a model

`gptr_providers()` lists configured routes and credential sources without making a request.
`gptr_models()` searches the catalog already available on disk. Neither listing proves that an
account can make a model request. `check = TRUE` probes provider reachability and CLI versions;
`refresh = TRUE` updates a catalog or asks a local server which models it has installed.

`gptr_providers(check_login = TRUE)` adds CLI-reported `signed in`, `not signed in` or `unknown`
states by running supported local status commands. It does not make a model request or verify
credentials online. This optional probe is separate from `check = TRUE`; both default to
`FALSE`, so the default listing starts no processes. A Codex API-key login can count as signed
in, so login status does not establish subscription billing.


``` r
gptr_providers()
gptr_models("sonnet")
gptr_models(provider = "openai")
gptr_providers(check = TRUE)
gptr_providers(check_login = TRUE)
```

Select a canonical `"provider/model"` reference to make the route explicit. Catalog aliases such
as `sonnet` also work. For a default, use `gptr_config(model = ..., .scope = "user")`; pass
`model = ...` to override it for one call. [Configuration](configuration.html) explains scope
and precedence.

### API providers

Obtain a key from the provider, then put it in the environment of your R process or an existing
private `.env` file. `gptr_env()` loads that file, registers values for redaction and reports names
and fingerprints. It leaves an existing environment variable alone unless `override = TRUE`.
Keep the file out of version control.

| Route | Credential variable | Example reference |
|---|---|---|
| Anthropic | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5"` |
| OpenAI | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `"openai/gpt-6-sol"` |
| Google Gemini | `GEMINI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | `"google/gemini-3.8-flash"` |
| OpenRouter | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | Choose a reference from `gptr_models(provider = "openrouter")` |
| Hosted System 1 | `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` (`jev-key` is a `.env` alias) | `"typesafe/jev-latest"` |


``` r
library(gptr)
gptr_env("~/keys/models.env")
gptr_config(model = "openai/gpt-6-sol", .scope = "user")
session = peter("Explain the relationship between mpg and wt.", mtcars)
session$text
```

A reply that falls silent for 90 seconds once it has started ends with a timeout; high-effort
reasoning on OpenAI or Google may need `options(gptr.idle_timeout = 300)`.

At first interactive use of a remote route, gptr asks you to acknowledge the data sent to it,
even with `context = "none"`: project instructions and environment details still go.
For unattended jobs, review `?gptr_egress` and acknowledge the specific provider beforehand at
user scope:


``` r
gptr_config(egress = utils::modifyList(gptr_config()$egress, list(openai = "ack")),
            .scope = "user")
```

Repeat this for each provider you use, including a custom provider or remote CLI route. Offline
providers and local loopback routes need no acknowledgment; Ollama is exempt only while its
local-only inference is on. Consent does not pre-approve tool actions. Read `?gptr_security`
before using sensitive data. `gptr_login("openrouter")`
offers an interactive login; `gptr_login("anthropic", method = "key")` offers masked key entry.
These credentials are separate from a command-line tool's sign-in.

An OpenAI-compatible service can use the existing completions adapter. Register its endpoint,
credential variable and the model metadata supplied by your service:


``` r
off = gptr_register(gptr_provider(
  "work", api = "openai-completions", base_url = "https://llm.example.org/v1",
  auth = "WORK_API_KEY",
  models = list(list(id = "work-model", context = 32000, max_output = 4000,
                     tool_call = TRUE))
))
peter("Summarize these data.", mtcars, model = "work/work-model")
off()  # remove this process-lifetime provider registration
```

Declare features only when your service supports them. Endpoint compatibility alone does not
establish tool, image or reasoning support. More built-in compatible routes appear in
`gptr_providers()`; `?gptr_provider` documents registration and compatibility fields.

### Azure OpenAI and Amazon Bedrock

The built-in Azure route reads `AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` and `AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`. Give the
resource endpoint, such as `https://your-resource.openai.azure.com`; gptr adds `/openai/v1`
and sends the key in the `api-key` header. The model sent to Azure is your deployment name.
Declare that deployment and its real capacities in provider settings:


``` r
gptr_env("~/keys/azure.env")  # AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY and AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT
azure_model = list(id = "analysis-chat", context = 32000, max_output = 4000,
                   tool_call = TRUE)
gptr_config(
  providers = list(azure = list(models = list(azure_model))),
  .scope = "session"
)
session = peter("Summarize these data.", mtcars, model = "azure/analysis-chat")
```

Replace `analysis-chat` and the limits with your deployment's metadata; declare `tool_call`
only when supported. Alternatively, `AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP` maps a declared model
id to its deployment using `model-id=deployment-name` pairs separated by commas.

The built-in Bedrock route uses `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` with the runtime's OpenAI-compatible
API. `AWS_REGION`, then `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, selects the region; the default is `us-east-1`.
Its endpoint is `https://bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com/openai/v1`. Choose a model your
account can use through that API and declare its id and capacities:


``` r
gptr_env("~/keys/bedrock.env")  # AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK and AWS_REGION
bedrock_model = list(id = "your-bedrock-model-id", context = 32000, max_output = 4000,
                     tool_call = TRUE)
gptr_config(
  providers = list(bedrock = list(models = list(bedrock_model))),
  .scope = "session"
)
session = peter("Summarize these data.", mtcars,
                model = "bedrock/your-bedrock-model-id")
```

Replace the illustrative metadata with your service's values. This built-in route does not
implement AWS SigV4 signing, AWS profile credentials or the general Bedrock Converse API.
An AWS credentials file alone therefore does not authenticate it, and the route does not imply
support for every Bedrock model. These remote providers need the egress acknowledgment
described above, using provider ids `azure` and `bedrock`.
For SigV4 and the Converse API, declare a provider with `api = "bedrock-converse"` (see
`?gptr_provider`). The bedrock-converse adapter does not request prompt caching, so each
request sends the full prompt at the uncached rate.

### Subscription command-line tools

Install and sign in to the `claude` or `codex` tool outside gptr, following that tool's own setup.
The executable must be on `PATH`, or you can give its path with the `gptr.cli_path` option.
Then choose `model = "claude-cli"` (alias `claude_code`) or `model = "codex"` (alias
`codex-cli`); `/model` in the console accepts the same names.


``` r
options(gptr.cli_path = list(claude = "/path/to/claude", codex = "/path/to/codex"))
gptr_providers(check = TRUE)
session = peter("Inspect the columns of mtcars.", mtcars, model = "codex")
```

These calls run a child process. The built-in `claude-cli` route uses the Claude Code CLI's
signed-in plan/OAuth authentication and refuses API-key billing. For API-key use, explicitly
choose the direct `anthropic` provider. The Codex route uses the CLI's active authentication and
billing. Live R access goes through gptr's MCP permission gate; Codex reaches it through a
small R relay that gptr ships, so the route needs no extra package. Codex's own shell does not
pass that gate: it runs commands within Codex's sandbox, which can read any file your account
can read (see `?gptr_security`). Both routes get the tools
your session declares to every model, and the console shows their tool calls and the first
line of each reasoning step while they run; Codex's answer arrives whole, since `codex exec`
does not stream text. First use asks for an acknowledgment. gptr
checks required CLI flags and rejects incompatible versions. The Claude plan route is experimental and opt-in; review `?gptr_security`
and the provider's terms before choosing it. On `claude-cli`, dollar figures (the footer,
`gptr_usage()`, block headers) are the CLI's API-equivalent estimate, not a charge; a `cost`
budget counts them.

`gptr_coach()` can run its sessions on either route, so a plan with no API key is enough to
coach a harness. On a plan it runs at most two sessions at once. When a plan limit is reached,
it starts nothing new and returns your starting harness. See
[Harnesses and coaching](tailor-and-coach.html).

### Local Ollama models

Run Ollama separately and install the model you intend to use. Discover the installed models,
then copy a returned reference into the call:


``` r
local_models = gptr_models(provider = "ollama", refresh = TRUE)
local_models
session = peter("Inspect mtcars and suggest a plot.", mtcars,
                model = "ollama/qwen3:1.7b")
```

The default server is `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`. For another local endpoint, configure its
`base_url` explicitly with `gptr_config(providers = list(ollama = list(base_url = ...)),
.scope = "user")`. gptr verifies installed-model capabilities and inference locality. Its
default `local_only = TRUE` rejects cloud selectors, remote markers and ambiguous locality;
it does not install, start or update Ollama, pull models or fall back to a cloud route.

Conversational models return sessions. Clef and Clef Flash are native decision models, require
Ollama 0.35.1 or later, and return logical, choice or score vectors. Their calls do not run an
agent conversation. See [Typed decisions](system-one.html). A local model does not keep a
later cloud call or network tool local.

## Work with a session

Ask for the analysis, then steer the same session:


``` r
session = peter("Fit mpg from wt in mtcars. Save the model as fit.", mtcars)
session |> peter("Explain how weight relates to fuel economy.")
session$text
```

`gptr_fork(session)` explicitly branches the conversation into a new session with an overlay
workspace. A model switch continues the existing history; a separate `peter()` call starts a new
session:


``` r
library(gptr)
fake = gptr_fake_provider(list("Weight is associated with lower fuel economy."))
other = gptr_fake_provider(list("An association does not establish causation."),
                           name = "other")
session = peter("Describe how mpg relates to wt.", mtcars, model = fake)
session |> peter("Add a caveat.", model = other)
#> An association does not establish causation.
#> idle . other/other-1 . 2 turns . 3.4k tokens . $0.0000 . s2ce6889652
```

## Put calls in functions and scripts

Inside a function, `peter()` works in the function's own frame, so new objects stay local.
Return the value Peter selected with ordinary R:


``` r
numeric_means = function(data) {
  session = peter("Compute and return each numeric-column mean.", data)
  session$value
}
```

<details>
<summary>Offline function example</summary>


``` r
numeric_means = function(data) {
  fake = gptr_fake_provider(list(
    list(tool = "r", input = list(code = paste(
      "numeric = vapply(data, is.numeric, logical(1))",
      "means = colMeans(data[numeric])",
      "gptr_return(means)", sep = "\n"
    ))),
    "The numeric-column means are ready."
  ))
  session = peter("Compute and return each numeric-column mean.", data,
                  model = fake, mode = auto)
  session$value
}
numeric_means(mtcars[c("mpg", "wt")])
#>      mpg       wt
#> 20.09062  3.21725
```

</details>

In a real script, replace the fake provider with an explicit model reference. Use `manual` when
a person can answer permissions; for an unattended job, choose appropriate permission rules
or an explicit mode before running it. `auto` still retains critical and secret guards.
A permission question with nobody present raises `gptr_error_permission` and carries the blocked
session as `e$session`.


``` r
session = tryCatch(
  peter("Fit mpg on wt and return the coefficients.", mtcars,
        model = "openai/gpt-6-sol", mode = auto, budget = list(cost = 1, turns = 10)),
  gptr_error_permission = function(e) {
    message(conditionMessage(e))
    e$session
  }
)
session$status
```

`gptr_usage(session)` reports tokens and costs. `gptr_prompt(session)` inspects the frozen prompt,
declared
tools, first message and token estimates; it does not report the current request's budgets.
Catalog prices and estimates are planning aids, and missing usage remains unknown. See
[Token efficiency](token-efficiency.html) for limits and
[Record, replay and export](script-as-history.html) for recording and replay that removes
repeated model calls.
